title: THEY DIDN’T RECOGNIZE HIM.
paragraphs: THEY DIDN’T RECOGNIZE HIM.
Not at first.

Two disciples walked the dusty road to Emmaus with heavy steps and shattered hope.
Jerusalem was behind them.
The cross was behind them.
And as far as they knew…
Jesus was behind them too.
Dead. Buried. Gone.
Then a stranger joined their walk.

Not ahead of them.
Not waiting at the destination.
Walking with them.

They talked about the rumors.
The empty tomb.
The confusion.
The heartbreak.
And the whole time…
It was Him.

The risen Christ.
The One they thought they lost.
But Luke tells us something strange:
“They were kept from recognizing Him.” — Luke 24:16
Imagine it.
The Savior of the world walking beside you, listening to your pain, explaining the Scriptures, stirring your heart…
And you still don’t see Him.
Sound familiar?
Sometimes Jesus walks beside us unnoticed.

When the prayer feels unanswered.
When the grief feels endless.
When the future looks like a closed door.

We whisper,
“Lord, where are You?”
But heaven might be whispering back:
“I’ve been walking with you the whole road.”
Then came the moment.
Dinner.
Bread.

Jesus took it…
blessed it…
broke it…
—and suddenly their eyes opened.
The stranger was the Savior.

The road that felt like defeat
became the road where resurrection walked beside them.
Friend, hear this carefully:

You may not recognize Him in the confusion.
You may not see Him in the delay.
You may not feel Him in the grief.
But Jesus is not absent.
He walks the Emmaus roads of broken hearts.

And when the moment is right,
He opens our eyes.
That is the Gospel.

The crucified Christ is alive.
The risen Savior still walks with sinners.
And hearts that burned in despair can burn again with hope.
So if today feels like an Emmaus road…
Keep walking.
Keep listening.
Keep inviting Him to stay.

Because the same Jesus who broke bread with those disciples
still reveals Himself today—
to anyone who turns to Him.
